segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הוֹרָה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ וְעָשָׂה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ – מִתְכַּפֵּר לוֹ בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ. הוֹרָה עִם הַצִּבּוּר וְעָשָׂה עִם הַצִּבּוּר – מִתְכַּפֵּר לוֹ עִם הַצִּבּוּר, שֶׁאֵין בֵּית דִּין חַיָּיבִין עַד שֶׁיּוֹרוּ לְבַטֵּל מִקְצָת וּלְקַיֵּים מִקְצָת, וְכֵן הַמָּשִׁיחַ, וְלֹא בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה עַד שֶׁיּוֹרוּ לְבַטֵּל מִקְצָת וּלְקַיֵּים מִקְצָת.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» If the anointed priest «issued a ruling by himself and performed» a transgression «by himself, he achieves atonement by himself» by bringing a bull as his sin-offering. If «he issued a ruling with the» general «public,» i.e., the Sanhedrin, «and performed» a transgression «with the» general «public,» i.e., the Jewish people, «he achieves atonement with the» general «public. As, the court is not liable unless» the judges «issue a ruling to nullify part» of a commandment «and to sustain part» of that commandment, «and likewise» with regard to the ruling of «the anointed» priest. «And» the court and the priest are «not» liable for a ruling «with regard to idol worship unless they issue a ruling to nullify part» of that commandment «and to sustain part» of it.

positions.claim: priest who ruled and acted with the public atones with the public; court and priest liable only for nullifying part of a mitzva, including idolatry
